brief:
# Build: voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T23:42:29.374Z
> can we have a setting to make it use Claude if Claude's connected

## What to build
Continue build "Voice listener: use Claude when connected (setting)" (voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 23:42):
"can we have a setting to make it use Claude if Claude's connected"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (14 left, ~2.1 h):
[ ] s1 (~8 min) Read the console-app-wake-word-voice-listener plugin: its scripted matcher, spoken wizard, command catalog loader, history store and settings. Read how the Claude badge works out connected or not (claude-session and llm capability axf.llm@1). Write a short design note in the plugin folder: where the Claude path plugs in, which catalog fields become tool schemas, the timeout and the fallback. Commit it.
[ ] s2 (~8 min) Add the setting 'Understand with Claude when connected' (key axf.voice.useClaude, default ON) and a timeout setting (default 8 s) to the plugin's settings. Put both in its Settings → Plugins sub-tab at the Basic level, and register them as control@1 targets and console-control setting addresses.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Server: write the catalog-to-tools converter. It turns each voice command in the API registry catalog into a Claude tool (name, description, input schema from the command's fields, a destructive flag, a personOnly flag). Approve and deny actions are never offered as tools. Add unit tests for the converter.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Server: write the Claude intent route (POST /api/plugins/<voice-listener>/understand). It takes the transcript and the session context, calls Claude through axf.llm@1 with the tools and a system prompt (pick one command, fill fields from what Brett said, ask only for what is missing, ask to confirm destructive actions), and returns {mode:'claude', command, args, ask?, confirm?}. Any error, timeout or badge-not-green returns {mode:'offline', reason}.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Server: add a multi-turn follow-up to the understand route. A follow-up answer from Brett is sent with the pending tool call so Claude fills only the missing fields. A destructive command returns confirm:true and runs only after a spoken yes. Add tests with a fake LLM covering: picks a command, asks for a missing field, confirm gate, timeout falls back to offline.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Web listener: when the setting is on and the Claude badge is green, send the transcript to the understand route first. Speak Claude's question or confirm prompt and loop the answers back to it. On offline, timeout or error, hand the same transcript to the existing scripted matcher and wizard without losing it.
[ ] s7 (~6 min) Approvals guard: make sure approve and deny never reach the Claude path. A spoken approval still needs the explicit 'approve' / 'deny' words and goes through the existing approvals-banner relay. Add a test that a Claude reply naming an approve tool is refused.
[ ] s8 (~8 min) UI: add a small 'offline mode' indicator on the listener's chip and panel, shown when Claude mode is on but the fallback handled the last command or the badge is not green. Use framework controls (fx-chip, tokens only) and register it as data-axf-target. API part: its state is readable at GET /api/plugins/<voice-listener>/state (mode, claudeConnected, lastFallbackReason).
[ ] s9 (~9 min) History: record mode (claude or scripted) and, for scripted, the fallback reason on every history entry (with a migration default of scripted for old entries). Show a mode tag column in the history grid and add a filter by mode. API part: GET history returns mode, and it can be filtered by mode.
[ ] s10 (~10 min) Full API: add REST get/set for the useClaude setting and timeout, a test-understand action (dry run on a phrase, returns what Claude would pick), and the state and history reads. Expose all of them as MCP plugin commands and console actions (voice.useClaude on|off, voice.understand.test). Add console_show deep links for the setting, the indicator and the history mode filter.
[ ] s11 (~9 min) CLI and voice: add `axf voice claude on|off|status|test "<phrase>"` and the AmberX voice commands 'use Claude for voice' and 'stop using Claude for voice' to the voice command catalog, both mapped to the same actions as REST and MCP. Add a parity test across REST, MCP, CLI and voice.
[ ] s12 (~8 min) Help, Shipped features and catalogs: write the plugin help page section (Claude mode, fallback, offline indicator, history mode, approvals stay spoken). Give the new commands and settings descriptions so the glossary index and the shipped-features ledger pick them up. Run catalog.mjs --check, check-console-control.mjs and check-control.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) UI Review: take desktop and phone shots of the setting, the offline indicator and the history mode tag. Make 3 options for the indicator (ui-choices@1 assets in plugins/<voice-listener>/assets/), and submit with review.mjs submit --choices --group 'voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected - <Mon D h:mm AM/PM>'.
[ ] s14 (~10 min) Tests, report and PR: run the plugin's test.py, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, plugin-lifecycle check and the tracker check. Write _claude/builds/reports/voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected.md, including how each feature is reached through REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Update the THREADS.md row, push the branch, open the PR (saying UI Review is waiting), and link it with builds-live.mjs link.
Read first: apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/, apps/console-web/plugins/claude-session/, _claude/builds/reports/voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected.md, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/plugin.json, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/web/, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/server/, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/server/claude_tools.py, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/test.py, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/server/routes.py, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/server/claude_intent.py, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/web/listener.ts, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/web/claudeMode.ts, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/server/history.py, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/web/History.tsx, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/commands.json, framework/cli/axf.mjs, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/cli.mjs, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/voice-commands.json, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/help/, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/README.md, apps/console-web/plugins/glossary-index/, apps/console-web/plugins/<voice-listener plugin>/assets/, apps/console-web/plugins/ui-review/, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.
